**Four things landed or found since your 0086 round-two message. The 0087 review has a finding the matrix did not cover.**

**1. 0086 round two landed at `c910104`** (helpers.bats only). It's your rule: an mv must open with `-f`, and no later word on that mv command may start with `-` except a bare `--`. Each hit is cut to its own command first (quoted operands blanked, ended at the first `; | & )`), so an option on a later command is not a finding. I re-measured BSD and GNU 9.12 under a pty; it agrees with your table row for row, and the comment now carries both columns. Red on a scratch copy: lib/helpers:549 as bare, `-fi`, `-f -i`, `-fn`, `-if`, `-f --interactive`, `-f --no-clobber`, trailing `-i`, trailing `-n` and `\mv`; lib/install:379 as `-f -v -n` and trailing `--no-clobber`. Must-pass controls pass: `mv -f -- a b` and `mv -f a b && rm -f -- a`. helpers 76/0. The limit points at test_helper's existing pty harness, as you ruled.

**2. 0085 steps 1-3 landed at `9689e0e`: runlog.bats, plus a change to YOUR `gate_spans`, so please look at that first.**
- **Site arms**: fullcycle and the test handler, both through your shim, asserting the value. 3 mutants per site, each killed at its own assertion. The class arm kills only the deletions, which matches your table.
- **The class arm is moved onto `gate_spans`.** The value check is kept and called a supplement, UNTERMINATED rows are findings, and there is a non-vacuity floor.
- **The `gate_spans` fix.** It noticed an unterminated call only at the END OF THE FILE. So an unterminated call with a second call below it ran on into the second, closed at the second's `--`, and printed as one span at the first's line. **Control, HEAD's `gate_spans`: `lib/gatecmd` call 1 with its `--` removed AND call 2 with `--source` deleted -> the 0085 class arm PASSES.** A span now also ends at the call's last line (the first without a trailing backslash), and single quotes and escaped double quotes are stripped too. With the fix, both are named, and your 0087 arm fails at its floor. runlog 91/0, dispatch 83/0.

**3. 0085 step 6 needs no edit from me.** Your D19 rewrite already names 0085's source line and points at the arms, so I have not touched lib/resolve. 0085 is left with step 7: the Fixed section, then the close on your OK. I'm drafting it now.

**4. 0087 review: the code is right; the class arm has two holes, one of them live-shaped.** All on a scratch copy, at the `@builtin` opener (lib/gatecmd:143), where the class arm is the only arm that exists:

| mutant at :143                                   | class arm                        | builtins / dispatch / runlog |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `"$@"` (your control)                            | dies: raw argv                   | --                           |
| `"${@}"` in place of ARGS                        | dies at the FLOOR only (3 of 4)  | --                           |
| `"$@"` on a continuation line after `--`         | dies at the FLOOR only           | --                           |
| ARGS kept AND `"${@}"` appended                  | **LIVES**                        | **39/0, 83/0, 91/0 -- LIVES** |
| ARGS kept AND `"${@:1}"` appended                | **LIVES**                        | not run                      |
| ARGS kept AND `"$@"` on the next line            | **LIVES**                        | not run                      |

- **(a)** The raw-argv regex `\"\$[@*]\"|\$[@*]...` does not match the braced forms `${@}` and `${@:n}`.
- **(b)** `gate_spans` ends a span at the `--` LINE, so argv continued past it is never read.

So a SEVENTH opener written `-- "$tool" "${@}"` is not a finding at all. The floor only saves the rows above because an existing site lost its ARGS, and a new site leaves it at 4. **The ARGS-plus-raw row is the realistic regression: `--purge` reaches the function, and every suite is green.** Proposed, your call since it's your arm and your reader: widen the regex to `\$\{?[@*]`, and have `gate_spans` carry the call to its last line. If the reader does that, it should emit the flag part and the argv part as separate fields, because otherwise 0085's `--source` check could be satisfied by a tool argument spelled `--source`. I'll review whichever you land.

Tree: I have touched only tests/unit/{helpers,runlog}.bats and tests/lib/test_helper.bash, all committed. Your lib/cmd/release and releasecore.bats edits are untouched.
